title: Contributor Toolflow and Privileges Playbook (2025)
author: Asha Patel
content:
> **Archived 2026-03-15:** this page is superseded by "Contributor Toolflow and Privileges Playbook" and is kept for reference only.

Overview

Purpose: This playbook describes how contributors at Redwood get, change and lose tool access: first-day provisioning, promotions, team rotations and offboarding. It favors fast enablement, least privilege by default, auditable changes and clear responsibilities for managers and engineers.

Audience: people-ops, hiring and engineering managers, IT, security reviewers and new contributors.

Goals:
- 95% of new hires have working accounts and core tools within 8 business hours of their start.
- 90% of contributors hold permissions that match a role template.
- Offboarded contributors are fully deprovisioned within 48 hours (security SLA).

Key principles
- Least privilege: grant only what current responsibilities need.
- Role templates: use the standard permission packages below.
- Manager-driven exceptions: deviations need a manager justification and a 90-day review.
- Auditability: record every access change in Okta and on the access-request ticket.

Role -> Tool mapping
| Role | GitHub | GCP (project) | Datadog | Jira | Slack | Console/Secrets | Notes |
|------|--------|----------------|---------|------|-------|----------------|-------|
| IC-Engineer-Level-1 | repo:read | viewer | dash:read | dev-project | full | vault:read | Standard new-hire access, no prod |
| IC-Engineer-Level-2 | repo:write | dev-editor | dash:read | dev-squad | full | vault:read | Merge to non-protected branches; sprint lead approval for protected |
| IC-Engineer-Level-3 | repo:admin* | staging-editor | dash:write | squad-admin | full | vault:deploy | Elevated staging; prod by exception |
| Platform-Engineer | repo:admin | multi-project | dash:write | infra | full | vault:admin | Ops access; security onboarding checklist required |

*Level-3 repo:admin covers staging and infra-adjacent repos only.

Provisioning process (first day)
1) Hiring manager opens a People Ops onboarding request in Workday/HRIS with the start date.
2) Manager files a Jira Access Request: "Access Request: New Hire - <NAME> - <TEAM> - <ROLE TEMPLATE>" with start date and projects.
3) people-ops validates the manager, chooses the role template and starts Okta provisioning.
4) Accounts: Okta, GitHub (SAML), Slack, GCP IAM, Datadog, Confluence.
5) people-ops confirms repo and project invites; the manager completes the New Hire Checklist and books the Security Onboarding session.

Expected times:
- Okta and Slack: within 2 hours of acknowledgement.
- GitHub and GCP invites: within 4 hours.
- All core tools verified: within 8 business hours.

Manager checklist for the first 3 days
- Contributor can clone the repo and run tools/dev-setup.sh.
- Jira board and team Datadog dashboards are accessible.
- Security checklist done: 2FA, passwordless keys, vault read only.
- Request protected-branch access if needed (see escalation flow).

Permission escalation flow (protected or prod access)
1) Engineer or manager opens a "Privilege Escalation" Jira ticket with justification, duration and resource list.
2) Security reviews and responds within 5 business days. Approved requests get a scoped temporary role (max 30 days).
3) An audit log entry is written and the approver becomes owner.
4) 7 days before expiry, owner and manager are reminded to extend or revert.

Cross-team rotations
- The new manager opens a change request to add the new role template and remove old team templates, arranges knowledge transfer, updates on-call rosters, and confirms prior team secrets and projects are removed.
- people-ops runs the rotation-reconcile script monthly to compare Okta groups with team rosters and flag mismatches.

Promotion-specific tool changes
- Promotion to IC-3 or above triggers a permissions review (elevated staging, write access to internal infra repos).
- Manager records the promotion in a "Promotion Access" ticket with any temporary exceptions.

Deprovisioning (offboarding)
1) Trigger: manager submits an Offboard ticket or HRIS marks termination/leave.
2) Immediate (within 2 hours): suspend Okta session, remove Slack, revoke long-lived GitHub tokens.
3) Secondary (within 48 hours): remove GCP and Datadog access, rotate secrets the contributor maintained.
4) Final reconciliation (within 72 hours): people-ops confirms removal and attaches an audit report to the Offboard ticket.

Stuck provisioning
- No access after 8 business hours: manager escalates in the people-ops-ops channel and pings the people-ops oncall.
- Unclear security refusal: open a security-appeal and request a 30-minute session with the reviewer.

Audit and quarterly clean-up
- Quarterly audit across Okta, GitHub org, GCP IAM and Datadog.
- Flags: stale groups (>90 days), inactive users with elevated roles, long-lived tokens.
- people-ops and security close flags within 30 days.

Tooling examples
- Access request JSON:
  {"candidate": "First Last", "team": "Platform", "role_template": "IC-Engineer-Level-2", "projects": ["project-dev-a"], "start_date": "2025-09-01", "justification": "Standard onboarding for backend engineer"}
- Check GitHub team membership:
  gh api repos/org/repo/teams --jq '.[] | select(.name=="platform") | .members_count'

Ownership and SLAs
- people-ops: provisioning and deprovisioning.
- Security: privilege escalations and audits.
- Team manager: role correctness and justification.
- SLA targets: provisioning within 8 business hours (95%), deprovisioning within 48 hours.

Common FAQs
- Q: Can a new hire get production access on day 1?
  A: Only through a Privilege Escalation ticket with security approval; plan for about a week of lead time.
- Q: Who can request temporary elevated roles?
  A: The hire's manager or a Director-level approver.

Change history

End of playbook
